text: Brom wanted to fight Ichabod. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod knew that if he fought Brom. <break time="0.8s" /> He would surely lose. <break time="0.8s" /> So Brom played tricks on him instead. <break time="0.8s" /> Stopping up his chimney. <break time="0.8s" /> And filling the schoolhouse with smoke. <break time="0.8s" /> He even trained a dog. <break time="0.8s" /> To whine in a silly way. <break time="0.8s" /> As if it were a rival singing teacher. <break time="0.8s" /> One autumn afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> A messenger arrived at the school. <break time="0.8s" /> With an invitation to a party. <break time="0.8s" /> At the Van Tassels. <break time="0.8s" /> Ichabod let the children go home. <break time="0.8s" /> An hour early. <break time="0.8s" /> And spent extra time. <break time="0.8s" /> Brushing his only black suit. <break time="0.8s" /> He borrowed an old plow horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Gunpowder. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was thin, half blind. <break time="0.8s" /> And still full of mischief. <break time="0.8s" /> At the farm. <break time="0.8s" /> The tables were covered. <break time="0.8s" /> With cakes, pies, and meats. <break time="0.8s" /> And Ichabod ate until he was full. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he danced with Katrina. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiling happily. <break time="0.8s" /> While Brom sat alone in a corner. <break time="0.8s" /> Sick with jealousy. <break time="0.8s" /> Later the guests told ghost stories. <break time="0.8s" /> And many of them were about the Headless Horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom said. <break time="0.8s" /> He had raced the Horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> To the church bridge. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the ghost vanished. <break time="0.8s" /> In a flash of fire.
